title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: arXiv:2610.21240v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose language model activations into sparse features, but prompt transformations designed to preserve the underlying request can redistribute activity across them. A feature change observed on one transformed prompt need not recur, and even a recurring change need not affect a downstream computation. We introduce the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS), which identifies large feature responses that recur in a consistent direction, and evaluate the resulting supports on variants excluded from selection. Across 27 pretrained SAEs spanning eight language models, the tested prompt transformations produce a reproducible redistribution profile on these excluded variants. We then separate recurring representation change from signed readout contribution and decision failure. translated_title: 稀疏自编码器中的表征再分配
translated_abstract: 稀疏自编码器将语言模型激活分解为稀疏特征，但旨在保持底层请求不变的提示变换可能会使激活活动在这些特征之间重新分布。在某一个变换后提示上观察到的特征变化未必会再次出现，即使是重复出现的变化，也未必会影响下游计算。我们引入了再分配敏感度分数，用以识别以一致方向重复出现的大幅特征响应，并在未参与选择过程的变体上评估由此得到的支持集。在涵盖八个语言模型的27个预训练SAE上，所测试的提示变换在这些被排除的变体上产生了可复现的再分布特征。随后，我们将重复出现的表征变化与带符号的读出贡献以及决策失败区分开来。对于固定的线性读出，一个精确分解展示了响应幅度、读出系数、方向对齐以及……
tldr: 该论文提出再分配敏感度分数（RSS）来识别在提示变换下以一致方向重复出现的大幅特征响应，并在涵盖八个语言模型的27个预训练SAE上验证了表征再分配的可复现性，同时将重复的表征变化与下游读出贡献及决策失败精确解耦。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS) to identify large feature responses that recur consistently under prompt transformations, demonstrates reproducible redistribution across 27 pretrained SAEs spanning eight language models, and precisely decomposes recurring representation changes from signed readout contributions and decision failures.
